title: My alarm rings for the roof 🌃
style_prompt: dark blue cinematic night, faceless silhouette, fog, minimal interior, no text, no watermark
hook_text: At 5:02 in the morning, my alarm said, wake up and go to the roof.

scenes.narration: At 5:02 in the morning, my alarm said, wake up and go to the roof.
I had never set it. The label said, roof. Repeat every day. Created six years ago.
I opened my camera roll to calm myself. The last photo was from 5:03 yesterday. The roof, at dawn.
The photo showed my feet, on the edge. The city below me. My shadow, stretched long.
I scrolled. Photo after photo. Every morning. Every dawn. Me, on the edge, facing out.
I do not remember any of it. I always wake up in bed. Warm. Rested. With cold feet.
Then I saw the newest photo. Taken minutes ago. Someone had been standing next to me on the roof.
The shape was thin. Tall. It held my hand. Its head tilted toward me, almost fondly.
I looked at my hands. They were cold. My slippers were wet with dew. And outside the window, the sky was just starting to turn grey.
The alarm rang again. This time, the label had changed. Come back up. You left someone waiting.
So tell me. Do you go up, or stay in bed?
